exam_name: ISTQB Certified Tester Test Automation Strategy

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Management approves automation expecting that the automated regression suite will uncover many new kinds of defects. The team knows the suite consists of repeated checks of existing behavior. What is the best strategic response?

options.A: Cancel the automation initiative, because a suite that only repeats checks brings no value to the organization
options.B: Agree with management, and promise that the suite will find more new defects than manual testing has ever found
options.C: Add random inputs to every automated test so that the suite is forced to find new kinds of defects each run
options.D: Set the expectation that regression automation detects unintended changes, and keep exploratory testing for new defects

questions.explanation: Regression suites are good at revealing side effects of change, not at discovering novel defects. Correcting expectations and combining automation with exploratory testing is realistic and keeps the benefits.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: A team records UI test scripts for nearly every scenario. Runs take hours, and many tests fail after small layout changes. Which strategic adjustment addresses this best?

options.A: Increase the wait times in every UI script so that layout changes are less likely to make the tests fail
options.B: Record even more UI scripts, so that any single failing script has a larger set of similar scripts around it
options.C: Move checks to lower levels where possible, such as unit and API tests, and keep only a few end-to-end UI tests
options.D: Stop all UI testing permanently, since UI tests can never be part of a sound automation strategy

questions.explanation: The pyramid suggests many fast, stable tests at the lower levels and few UI tests. Shifting checks down reduces runtime and fragility, while keeping a small set of end-to-end tests for integration confidence.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: The system under test offers only a user interface with dynamically generated element identifiers, so automated tests break often. What is the most effective long-term strategy?

options.A: Work with developers to add testability, such as stable identifiers and test interfaces
options.B: Switch to image-based comparison of screenshots, which never breaks when the application changes
options.C: Accept the situation and add a full-time engineer to fix the broken locators after every build
options.D: Ask the testers to memorize the changing identifiers and update the scripts by hand each morning

questions.explanation: Testability is a cost driver for automation. Building stable identifiers and interfaces into the SUT removes a root cause of fragility, whereas workarounds keep paying the maintenance cost.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Two candidate tests could be automated first. Test X is executed daily, is stable and takes 30 minutes manually. Test Y is executed twice a year, changes frequently and takes 3 hours manually. Which should be automated first, and why?

options.A: Test Y, because tests that change frequently are the ones that automation handles best
options.B: Test Y, because it takes longer to run manually and therefore saves more per single execution
options.C: Neither, because a test can only be automated once it has been executed by hand at least 100 times
options.D: Test X, because frequent execution of a stable test returns the automation investment quickly

questions.explanation: Return on investment depends on how often a test runs and how stable it is. Test X repeats often and rarely changes, so its savings accumulate quickly and maintenance stays low.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Building an automated test takes 45 hours. One manual execution takes 5 hours, and one automated execution needs 0.5 hours of attended effort. Ignoring maintenance, after roughly how many executions does the automation break even?

options.A: About 100 executions, because the build effort must be multiplied by two for a break-even
options.B: About 90 executions, because 45 divided by 0.5 hours per automated run equals 90 executions
options.C: About 9 executions, because 45 divided by 5 hours per manual run equals 9 executions
options.D: About 10 executions, because each automated run saves 4.5 hours and 45 divided by 4.5 is 10

questions.explanation: Each automated run saves 5 minus 0.5, which is 4.5 hours. Dividing the 45-hour investment by that saving gives 10 runs. Real calculations should add maintenance effort, which raises the break-even point.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: A team plans to automate all functional checks and to stop exploratory testing to save effort. What is the most valid concern?

options.A: Automated checks confirm only what was anticipated, so dropping exploratory testing loses surprises
options.B: Exploratory testing is prohibited in agile teams, so the team is right to remove it from its plan
options.C: Automated checks are always more expensive than exploratory testing, so the plan will increase costs
options.D: Exploratory testing can be replaced completely by increasing the number of automated tests

questions.explanation: Scripted automation verifies expected behavior. Exploratory testing brings human curiosity and learning that finds surprising problems, so the two complement each other.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: In an agile team, automation for new features is planned for a later sprint, and the backlog of unautomated stories grows. Which strategic approach is more sustainable?

options.A: Assign a separate team to automate stories after release, and accept that features are untested until then
options.B: Reduce the number of stories per sprint until the backlog of unautomated stories disappears by itself
options.C: Postpone automation until the end of the project, when the requirements are final and stable
options.D: Include creating or updating automated tests in the definition of done so that automation keeps pace with development

questions.explanation: Making automation part of the definition of done keeps tests current and spreads the effort, preventing an ever-growing automation backlog.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: An old system has a two-week manual regression cycle and no automation. The team has limited capacity. Where should the strategy start?

options.A: Automate critical, stable paths such as smoke and key business flows, then expand by value
options.B: Wait until the system is rewritten before any automation is started
options.C: Try to automate the entire two-week regression cycle before releasing anything else
options.D: Automate the rarely used features first because they are the least likely to change

questions.explanation: Starting small with critical, stable flows delivers early value and learning within limited capacity. Attempting everything at once or waiting delays benefits and increases risk.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Automated checks on a report compare full output text, but they fail intermittently because the output contains timestamps and generated IDs. What is the best fix?

options.A: Repeat the check until the timestamps and IDs happen to be identical between two runs
options.B: Remove the check so that the report is no longer verified by any automated test
options.C: Freeze the system clock of the production environment so that timestamps never change
options.D: Ignore or mask the variable parts in the comparison, or compare only the relevant fields

questions.explanation: Variable content is not part of the expected result. Masking it or comparing meaningful fields keeps the check stable and focused on real behavior.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: An organization must choose between three tools. Stakeholders disagree, and one team simply prefers the tool it already knows. Which approach supports a sound decision?

options.A: Let the loudest team decide, since delays in the decision are more costly than selecting a poor tool
options.B: Choose the tool with the longest feature list, since it is likely to satisfy every possible future need
options.C: Choose the cheapest tool, because license cost is the only criterion that can be measured objectively
options.D: Define weighted criteria based on needs, evaluate the tools against them with a proof of concept, and compare the scores

questions.explanation: A criteria-based evaluation with a proof of concept links the decision to actual needs and produces comparable evidence. Feature counts, price alone or preference do not.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: A team of manual testers with little programming experience must start automating. Which resource decision best balances speed and long-term maintainability?

options.A: Use keyword-driven testing with reusable keywords built by a few engineers, and train testers to compose tests
options.B: Require every tester to write complex framework code from the first week, regardless of experience
options.C: Buy a tool that generates unreadable scripts by recording, and never review or refactor them
options.D: Hire a large group of external programmers and remove the testers from the automation work entirely

questions.explanation: A layered approach lets skilled engineers provide reusable building blocks while testers apply their domain knowledge, which balances skills and maintainability. Unrealistic demands or unreviewed recordings do not.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: A manager argues that an open-source tool is free, so no budget is needed. Which response best reflects total cost of ownership?

options.A: Only the license cost matters, so open-source and commercial tools should be considered equal
options.B: Open-source tools avoid license fees, but budget is still needed for training, integration, support and maintenance
options.C: The manager is correct, since open-source tools never require any effort beyond the download
options.D: Open-source tools are always more expensive than commercial tools in every possible situation

questions.explanation: Total cost includes people, infrastructure and support, not just licenses. Open-source tools shift costs rather than remove them.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: One developer built the in-house automation framework and left no documentation. Several teams depend on it. What is the best strategic response?

options.A: Document the framework, share ownership, and consider a well-supported standard framework
options.B: Delete the framework and ask each team to write its own scripts from the beginning
options.C: Ask the teams to stop using the framework until the developer can be found
options.D: Continue as before, because the developer might return to explain everything when needed

questions.explanation: Knowledge concentrated in one person is a serious risk. Sharing ownership, documenting and possibly moving to a supported standard reduces dependence and improves maintainability.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: A product has a web application and native mobile apps. The team considers one tool for everything versus separate specialized tools. Which is the most balanced consideration?

options.A: Choose the tool that the vendor's sales representative recommends, since vendors know the products best
options.B: Always choose separate tools for each platform, because a shared skill set has no value
options.C: Weigh a shared approach and skill set against each tool's fit per platform, and validate with a proof of concept
options.D: Always choose one tool for all platforms, because having two tools is never acceptable

questions.explanation: Consolidation lowers training and maintenance cost, but a tool must also handle each platform well. A proof of concept shows the true trade-off.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: The vendor of the organization's automation tool announces that the product will reach end of life in two years. Which strategic action is most appropriate?

options.A: Immediately delete all automated tests, because they cannot be used after the announcement
options.B: Buy additional licenses for ten years so that the product can be used forever
options.C: Plan a migration path, add an abstraction layer to limit tool-specific code, and evaluate replacements
options.D: Ignore the announcement until the last month before the end of life is reached

questions.explanation: Early planning and an abstraction layer make migration cheaper. Ignoring the announcement or deleting tests loses value, and licenses do not extend support.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: A team compares building an in-house device lab with using a cloud device farm. Usage is unpredictable, and data on the devices is not sensitive. Which is the better fit?

options.A: A cloud device farm, because usage-based cost and access to many devices suit unpredictable demand
options.B: An in-house lab with a single device, because one device gives the same coverage as many devices
options.C: Neither, because mobile testing cannot be automated on real devices
options.D: An in-house lab, because owning devices is always cheaper regardless of how rarely they are used

questions.explanation: Variable demand favors pay-per-use capacity, and non-sensitive data reduces security objections. A private lab pays off mainly with steady, high utilization or strict data restrictions.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Testers want to copy production data into the automation environment because generating data is slow. Privacy rules restrict use of personal data. Which resource strategy is best?

options.A: Use masked or synthetic data generated by a controlled process, and keep only what the tests need
options.B: Copy the production data unchanged, since testers are trusted employees
options.C: Use the same few records in every test, and never refresh them regardless of tests that change them
options.D: Stop all testing that requires personal data, because it can never be tested legally

questions.explanation: Masked or synthetic data preserves usefulness while respecting privacy rules. Unmasked copies violate policy, and static records cause interference and fragile tests.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Automated tests pass on a developer's machine but fail intermittently on the shared test environment, where several teams deploy at will. What is the best long-term strategy?

options.A: Lower the number of tests in the suite until failures on the shared environment become rare
options.B: Provide isolated, reproducible environments, such as containers, so that runs cannot interfere
options.C: Run all suites at night only, and ignore the failures that occur during the working day
options.D: Ask the teams to coordinate by phone and rerun failed tests until they pass on the shared setup

questions.explanation: Isolation and reproducibility remove interference as a root cause of intermittent failures. Reruns, fewer tests or ignoring failures conceal the problem.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Cloud test environments are left running around the clock, and costs are rising although tests only run during working hours. Which measure is most appropriate?

options.A: Automate scheduling so that environments start when needed and are shut down or removed when idle
options.B: Turn off the environments permanently and ask teams to test on production instead
options.C: Increase the size of every environment so that tests finish in half the time
options.D: Keep the environments running and reduce the number of tests to lower costs

questions.explanation: Paying only for time in use is a major advantage of cloud resources. Scheduling and automatic clean-up cut idle cost without harming test capacity.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Tests run in parallel and fail because they modify the same customer records. What is the most suitable design response?

options.A: Run tests one at a time forever, even though the suite then takes many hours
options.B: Let the tests retry until each of them happens to use a record that another test is not using
options.C: Give each test or worker its own data, or create unique data per test, so parallel runs do not collide
options.D: Remove the assertions that check the customer records, so that collisions no longer cause failures

questions.explanation: Independent test data allows safe parallel execution. Serializing everything or weakening checks sacrifices speed or value, and retries hide the real defect in the design.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: The payment provider's test system is often unavailable and rate limited, which causes many automated checkout tests to fail. What is the best strategy?

options.A: Remove all checkout tests from the suite, because payments cannot be tested automatically
options.B: Use service virtualization or a test double for most runs, and keep a few checks against the real sandbox
options.C: Process real customer payments during test runs to make sure the provider always responds
options.D: Continue using the provider's system for all tests and ask the provider to be more reliable

questions.explanation: Simulating the dependency isolates the tests from availability and limits, while a small number of checks against the real sandbox verify the integration. Real payments are unacceptable.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Tests pass in the test environment but a defect appears in staging because a dependent service runs at a different version. Which strategy best reduces such surprises?

options.A: Test only in production, where every version is assumed to be correct and consistent
options.B: Manage configuration as code and keep versions and settings aligned across environments
options.C: Ask testers to remember which versions are installed in each of the environments
options.D: Avoid using staging for any kind of testing, and rely on developer machines instead

questions.explanation: Versioned, code-managed configuration makes differences visible and repeatable, reducing environment-specific defects. Memory or avoiding stages does not.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: The performance test environment has one quarter of the capacity of production. The team wants to declare that production will handle the peak load if the test passes. What is the best position?

options.A: Ignore the results, because performance cannot be tested outside production in any case
options.B: Multiply the response time by four and treat the result as an exact production figure
options.C: Treat the result as indicative, and use models or extra checks to judge capacity, since scaling is not linear
options.D: Accept the result as proof, because a smaller environment is always sufficient to represent production

questions.explanation: A scaled-down environment gives useful trends but not exact predictions, because bottlenecks and scaling do not always behave linearly. Results must be interpreted with care and supported by other evidence.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Database passwords and API keys used by tests are stored in the automation scripts in the repository. What is the best remedy?

options.A: Encode the secrets in Base64 so that they cannot be read in the repository
options.B: Move the secrets to a secrets manager or protected pipeline variables, and rotate the exposed credentials
options.C: Send the secrets by email to each tester when a run is started
options.D: Keep the secrets in the scripts but restrict the repository to a few trusted users

questions.explanation: Secrets should never live in source code. A secrets manager controls access and rotation, whereas Base64 is not protection and emailing secrets spreads them.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: A nightly suite fails because the test environment was unavailable for two hours, but nobody noticed until the morning. Which improvement is most effective?

options.A: Tell testers to check the environment personally at midnight every day
options.B: Remove the nightly suite and run tests only when the environment is known to be available
options.C: Run the suite twice each night so that at least one run finds the environment available
options.D: Add environment health checks and monitoring with alerts, and run checks before the suite starts

questions.explanation: Automated health checks and alerts detect problems early, prevent meaningless runs and reduce time to recovery. Manual midnight checks or duplicate runs are unreliable and wasteful.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A delivery pipeline runs every automated test in a single stage that takes three hours, and developers rarely wait for the result. How should the stages be organized?

options.A: Keep one stage but rename it so that the delay looks shorter to the developers
options.B: Run fast unit and smoke checks first, then integration and system tests in later stages
options.C: Run the slowest tests first because they are the most likely to find problems
options.D: Remove the pipeline stages and run all tests manually before each release

questions.explanation: Staging from fast to slow gives quick feedback on most problems, and reserves long-running tests for later. A single long stage delays feedback and encourages ignoring results.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A flaky test fails randomly and blocks the release gate. Teams start rerunning the pipeline until it passes. Which policy is best?

options.A: Leave the test in the gate, and allow anyone to override the gate whenever it fails
options.B: Quarantine the flaky test, track it as a defect with an owner, and restore it once fixed
options.C: Increase the number of automatic reruns to ten so that the test eventually passes
options.D: Delete the test permanently, without checking which risk or feature it was covering

questions.explanation: Quarantining protects the gate's credibility while keeping the problem visible until it is fixed. Overrides, deletion or more reruns hide the risk or erode trust in the gate.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A release candidate has two failed automated tests, and the schedule is tight. What is the most appropriate way to decide?

options.A: Release, because two failed tests out of thousands are always insignificant
options.B: Never release while any automated test fails, whatever the cause or the risk
options.C: Analyze the failures, assess the risk with stakeholders, and record the decision
options.D: Delete the two failing tests and release, since there are then no failures

questions.explanation: Failures differ in cause and impact, so a documented, risk-based decision made with stakeholders is better than automatic rules in either direction, or hiding the failures.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Releases are now daily, but the full regression suite needs eight hours. Which strategy keeps quality feedback timely?

options.A: Select tests by change and risk, for example via impact analysis, and run the full suite nightly
options.B: Skip regression testing on daily releases and rely on users to report problems
options.C: Run the full suite manually before each release, even if that blocks the release each day
options.D: Reduce the suite to the ten easiest tests and treat them as full regression

questions.explanation: Impact-based selection keeps the fast feedback loop relevant to each change, while the complete suite still runs on a slower cadence. Skipping or trimming to easy tests loses coverage.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A pilot finished, but stakeholders argue about whether it succeeded, because no success criteria had been defined. What should be done in the next pilot?

options.A: Avoid pilots in the future because they only cause disagreements
options.B: Ask the vendor of the tool to decide whether the pilot succeeded
options.C: Define measurable success criteria before the pilot starts, and agree them with stakeholders
options.D: Decide success afterwards by choosing the measures that make the results look best

questions.explanation: Criteria agreed in advance make the outcome objective and comparable. Choosing measures afterward or letting the vendor judge undermines credibility.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A shared framework has a new major version, and thirty teams use the old one. What is the best rollout approach?

options.A: Never upgrade the framework, because upgrades always break the automation of the teams
options.B: Publish a migration guide, support both versions for a period, and let teams migrate in stages
options.C: Force all teams to upgrade on the same day and remove the old version immediately
options.D: Release the new version without notice and let teams find the changes themselves

questions.explanation: Staged migration with guidance and a support period reduces disruption while keeping the framework current. Forced, silent or no upgrades create risk or stagnation.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A feature is released behind a feature toggle and is switched on for a small user group first. Which testing consideration follows for automation?

options.A: Only the toggle-on state matters, because the toggle-off state can never be seen by any user
options.B: Tests should ignore the toggle and run whichever state the environment happens to be in
options.C: Toggles make automation impossible, so all tests must be executed manually
options.D: Tests should cover both toggle states where relevant and control the toggle configuration

questions.explanation: Both states can be visible in production, and uncontrolled toggles make results unreproducible, so tests should set and cover the relevant states explicitly.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: An urgent hotfix must be released within hours. The full regression suite needs a day. What is the most sensible approach?

options.A: Release without any testing, since hotfixes are exempt from quality checks
options.B: Run a pre-agreed subset covering the fix and top risks, then the full regression later
options.C: Run a random selection of tests, and document the release as fully regressed
options.D: Delay the hotfix for a day until the full suite has finished in every case

questions.explanation: A risk-based subset gives fast, meaningful assurance under time pressure, with the full suite completing later. Random selection or no testing offers false or no assurance.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Auditors ask for proof that specific tests were run and passed for a released version. Which practice best supports this?

options.A: Rely on the memory of team members about which tests were run for each version
options.B: Store results with build and version identifiers, retained per the agreed period
options.C: Print the overall pass rate on a slide and archive the slide for the audit
options.D: Keep only the latest run and overwrite the earlier results every night

questions.explanation: Traceable, retained results tied to versions provide evidence on demand. Overwriting, memory or summaries do not.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: A small central automation team is overwhelmed by requests from ten product teams, and delivery is delayed. Which structural change is most effective?

options.A: Dissolve the central team and assign all of its members to one product team
options.B: Enable product teams via shared frameworks and coaching, with the central team as experts
options.C: Tell the product teams to stop asking for automation until the backlog is gone
options.D: Add more requests to the central team so that its backlog is fully visible

questions.explanation: Enabling teams to self-serve removes the bottleneck while keeping consistency and expertise. Ignoring demand or giving all people to one team does not solve it.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Manual testers resist automation because they fear losing their jobs. Which management response is most constructive?

options.A: Exclude testers from the initiative and let external staff do all of the work
options.B: Deny that any change to roles will occur, and avoid discussing automation with the testers
options.C: Explain the vision, involve testers in the automation, and provide reskilling
options.D: Announce that testers who do not learn programming this month will be dismissed

questions.explanation: Involvement, transparency and training turn fear into participation and keep valuable domain knowledge. Threats, exclusion or denial increase resistance and lose expertise.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: A candidate for the automation engineer role writes excellent code but shows little interest in test design or risk. Which view is most appropriate?

options.A: Reject every candidate who can write code, since programmers cannot become testers
options.B: Engineers need testing insight as well as engineering skills, so assess both or develop the gap
options.C: Test design is unimportant in automation, since tools decide which tests are worth running
options.D: Coding skill alone is sufficient, because test design can be added later by anyone

questions.explanation: Good automation depends on knowing what to test and why. Both skills matter, and gaps should be identified and addressed through hiring mix or development.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Each team built a different automation framework, and nobody is responsible for overall consistency. Which role would help address this?

options.A: A test automation architect who defines common architecture, guidelines and reusable components
options.B: An additional manual tester for each team who runs the tests by hand
options.C: A tool vendor representative who decides the framework for each team
options.D: A recruitment specialist who selects the programming language for each team

questions.explanation: Someone must own the architecture and standards so that teams reuse solutions, avoid duplication and keep automation maintainable. That is the architect role.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: An organization has ten product teams with different maturity levels and a small group of automation experts. Which structure is most likely to work well?

options.A: No structure at all, so that each person automates whatever they want
options.B: A fully central team that performs all of the automation work for every team
options.C: A single team that works exclusively on documentation and never on tests
options.D: A hybrid: engineers embedded in teams, plus a central group or community for standards

questions.explanation: A hybrid keeps automation close to the product work while sharing expertise and standards centrally. Pure central or unstructured models have bottleneck and consistency issues.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Skilled automation engineers keep moving into developer roles, and the team loses knowledge. What is the most appropriate response?

options.A: Prohibit any employee from changing roles, whatever their own interests are
options.B: Reduce salaries in automation roles so that fewer people join and leave
options.C: Offer a career path with growth opportunities, and make knowledge sharing part of the work
options.D: Stop hiring automation engineers and rely only on the manual testers in place

questions.explanation: A career path with growth options improves retention, and documented, shared knowledge limits the damage from any departure. Prohibitions or lower pay make things worse.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Developers say that testing and automation are the QA team's job, and they do not fix flaky tests in their areas. Which cultural strategy is best?

options.A: Promote shared responsibility for quality, such as test work in the definition of done
options.B: Hire more QA staff so that developers never need to think about tests
options.C: Assign all blame for failing tests to the QA team so that developers can focus on features
options.D: Prevent developers from seeing the test results to avoid arguments

questions.explanation: Quality is a team responsibility. Shared goals, metrics and working agreements bring developers into automation, unlike blame, secrecy or handing everything to QA.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A manager wants to reward the team with the largest number of automated scripts. What is the main danger of using this as a key metric?

options.A: It reduces the amount of maintenance because more scripts share the same failures
options.B: It encourages quantity over value, so low-value or duplicated scripts may be created
options.C: It is impossible to count scripts, so the metric cannot be calculated at all
options.D: It guarantees that the most valuable tests are automated first

questions.explanation: Counting scripts rewards volume and can distort behavior. Metrics should reflect value, such as risk covered, effort saved or defects found early.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: About 8 percent of automated test runs fail for no clear reason and pass on rerun. The team spends much time investigating them. Which approach is best?

options.A: Identify root causes such as timing, data or environment issues, fix them, and track the flaky rate
options.B: Configure the pipeline to rerun every failing test until it passes and ignore the first failure
options.C: Delete all tests that have ever failed once, to make the suite reliable
options.D: Accept the flakiness as normal and stop investigating failed tests

questions.explanation: Flaky tests erode trust and waste effort. Finding and fixing causes and tracking the rate improves reliability, while masking or deleting removes information or coverage.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Analysis shows that 60 percent of the automation team's time goes into fixing broken scripts after UI changes. Which improvement has the best long-term effect?

options.A: Delete the scripts that break most often and do not replace them with anything
options.B: Improve abstraction, such as page objects, so changes are made in one place
options.C: Tell the developers never to change the user interface again after release
options.D: Hire more people to fix the scripts faster after every interface change

questions.explanation: Layered design localizes the effect of change and reduces maintenance permanently. More staff treats symptoms, and freezing the UI or deleting scripts is unrealistic or loses coverage.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A backlog of unanalyzed failed tests builds up, and nobody feels responsible. What should be established?

options.A: Clear ownership and a triage process with agreed response times for failed automated tests
options.B: A separate dashboard that hides failed tests from most people
options.C: A requirement that only the person who wrote the test may ever look at its failures
options.D: A rule that failed tests are ignored after seven days

questions.explanation: Ownership and a triage routine make sure failures are investigated promptly and correctly routed to defects, script fixes or environment work. Hiding or ignoring failures erodes value.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Developers stop reading automated results because many reported failures turn out to be script or environment problems. How can trust be restored?

options.A: Mark every failure as a product defect so that developers take them seriously
options.B: Reduce false positives by fixing causes, separating failures by type in reports, and communicating improvements
options.C: Ask developers to read the results more carefully and accept that many failures are noise
options.D: Stop publishing results so that developers are not distracted

questions.explanation: Trust depends on results being reliable and understandable. Lowering noise and clearly separating cause categories restores credibility, whereas hiding or mislabeling failures destroys it.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: An executive asks for a report on the automation program, and an engineer asks for details of failing tests. Which reporting approach is most suitable?

options.A: Send the same detailed log to everyone, since all readers need every detail
options.B: Provide reports only to the engineers, because executives should not see automation data
options.C: Provide only a green or red status to everyone, whatever they need to know
options.D: Tailor reports to the audience: trends and business impact for executives, details for engineers

questions.explanation: Different audiences need different levels of detail. Tailored reporting keeps information useful and supports decisions at each level.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: The regression suite has grown, and the run takes six hours, which slows feedback. Which options belong in an improvement plan?

options.A: Running the suite only once a year to avoid the delay
options.B: Parallel execution, removing duplicated or low-value tests, and selecting tests by risk or impact
options.C: Adding more tests of the same kind and running them one after another
options.D: Removing all logging and reporting, so the suite finishes faster and no one sees results

questions.explanation: Speed can be improved by using more parallelism, pruning tests and choosing tests smartly. Adding tests or removing reporting or frequency does not solve the feedback problem.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A team reports 90 percent code coverage from automated tests and concludes that quality is assured. What is the best comment?

options.A: Coverage of 90 percent means that 90 percent of all defects have been removed
options.B: Coverage is meaningless and should never be measured by any team at any time
options.C: Coverage above 80 percent guarantees that there are no defects in the remaining code
options.D: Coverage shows which code ran, not whether behavior was verified, so add other measures

questions.explanation: Executed code is not necessarily checked by meaningful assertions. Coverage is a useful indicator, but it needs to be combined with measures of what the tests actually verify.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: The whole automation effort depends on one enthusiastic champion who drives the work. Which strategic step best increases the chance of lasting success?

options.A: Replace the champion after a year to avoid the person becoming too important
options.B: Reduce the scope of the initiative to what the champion can do alone
options.C: Secure management support and shared ownership so that the initiative does not depend on one person
options.D: Keep the champion as the only owner, so that decisions are quick and consistent

questions.explanation: Sustained success needs organizational backing and several people who own and understand the work. Depending on one person creates a fragile initiative.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Stakeholders want fast delivery, high coverage and low cost from automation, and the goals conflict. What is the best way to handle this in the strategy?

options.A: Choose the objective that is easiest to measure, and ignore the others
options.B: Prioritize objectives with stakeholders based on business goals and risk
options.C: Promise to achieve all three goals at the same time without any compromise
options.D: Let each team decide privately which objective it will follow

questions.explanation: Objectives can conflict, so they should be ranked with the stakeholders and the resulting trade-offs made visible. Unrealistic promises or private choices cause disappointment and inconsistency.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: A financial calculation produces results that testers cannot easily predict, so automated checks lack an oracle. Which approach is most practical?

options.A: Compare the results to random numbers and accept small differences in all cases
options.B: Skip automation for calculations, and accept that they will never be verified
options.C: Use an independent reference calculation, or check properties that must always hold
options.D: Use the output of the system under test as the expected result of each check

questions.explanation: Independent references or invariant checks give a meaningful oracle. Using the SUT's own output as the expectation only confirms that it behaves as it did.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Requirements for a new product change every week. The team wants to start UI automation right away. Which strategy is most sensible?

options.A: Automate the whole UI now and rewrite the scripts every week as the requirements change
options.B: Wait until the product is released and the requirements have stopped changing
options.C: Start with stable lower-level and API checks, and delay broad UI automation until it stabilizes
options.D: Automate only the parts of the UI that the product owner has said will change most often

questions.explanation: Volatile interfaces make UI automation costly to maintain. Stable lower levels give value with less rework, and UI automation can grow when the design settles.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: A team defines the objective "get feedback on each code change within 15 minutes". What is the implication for the automation strategy?

options.A: The commit-triggered suite must be small and fast, and slower tests must move to later stages
options.B: Feedback will be provided manually by testers after they have reviewed the code
options.C: All available tests must be part of the commit-triggered suite, regardless of duration
options.D: The objective can be met by running tests only once each week

questions.explanation: A time-to-feedback goal shapes test selection and structure: fast, reliable checks per change, with broader suites on a slower schedule.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: The first pilot scope is a complex module with unstable requirements and many integrations. The pilot struggles. What should the next pilot look like?

options.A: An even larger area, so that the pilot covers more of the product
options.B: No pilot, and a direct rollout to all teams to save time
options.C: A small, representative area with stable requirements and clear success criteria
options.D: A module chosen because nobody understands it, to test the tool as hard as possible

questions.explanation: Pilots should be manageable and representative so they can succeed and provide reliable lessons. An overly complex scope produces noise instead of insight.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Tests verify in detail how a third-party library formats its dates, and they break whenever the library is updated. Which strategy is better?

options.A: Stop updating the library forever, so that the tests never break
options.B: Delete the tests and never check any behavior that involves the library
options.C: Add more detailed tests of the library so that all of its behavior is covered
options.D: Verify your system's use of the library through its contract, not the library's internals

questions.explanation: Tests should concentrate on what your team owns and depends on. Re-testing a supplier's internals creates maintenance without much value, while contract-level checks cover the integration.

questions.domain: Introduction and Objectives for Test Automation Strategy
questions.question: Management wants to see full automation benefits within two sprints, though the team is new to automation. Which response is most appropriate?

options.A: Refuse to report any results until the automation is completely finished
options.B: Agree to the two-sprint deadline and cut corners on design to meet it
options.C: Propose phased goals with early, achievable results and a realistic timeline for larger benefits
options.D: Promise a larger benefit than requested, to increase management's confidence

questions.explanation: Phased, realistic goals show progress while managing expectations. Rushing or over-promising leads to poor design and lost credibility.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Thirty testers use a licensed tool, each for about three hours per day, and not always at the same times. Which license approach is most economical?

options.A: Floating licenses sized for peak concurrent use, with some headroom
options.B: Thirty named licenses, one for each tester
options.C: One license per team, shared by passing the login details around
options.D: A single license for the whole company, used in turns

questions.explanation: Floating licenses match usage that is spread over time. Named licenses pay for idle capacity, and sharing credentials or a single license violates terms and blocks work.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: A team wants to assign automation tasks efficiently to its members, who have different backgrounds. Which resource practice helps most?

options.A: Assign tasks alphabetically by the name of each team member
options.B: Keep a skills overview, match tasks to strengths, and plan development for gaps
options.C: Assign every task to the most experienced person to be safe
options.D: Give the hardest tasks to the newest member so they learn quickly

questions.explanation: Knowing who can do what enables better assignment and highlights training needs. Arbitrary or concentrated assignment wastes talent and creates risk.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: External contractors build most of the automation on a fixed-term contract. What should the organization ensure regarding its resources?

options.A: That the internal team stays out of the work to avoid disturbing the contractors
options.B: That the contract ends immediately after the first working script is delivered
options.C: That knowledge is transferred, and that the code and documentation are owned by and accessible to the organization
options.D: That the contractors keep the code on their own systems so that the organization cannot change it

questions.explanation: Contractors leave, so the organization needs access, ownership and understanding to maintain what was built. Isolation from the work creates dependency.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: A suite takes six hours on one machine. Running on four machines would take about 1.5 hours, at additional infrastructure cost. What is the sound way to decide?

options.A: Always buy the additional machines, because speed is more valuable than cost in every case
options.B: Buy machines in proportion to the number of testers, whatever the suite duration
options.C: Never buy additional machines, since a long-running suite is always acceptable
options.D: Compare the cost of the extra machines with the value of faster feedback and the time saved for the team

questions.explanation: Resource decisions weigh cost against the benefit of shorter feedback. There is no universal answer, so the trade-off should be made on the basis of value.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: A tool candidate looks capable, but it cannot connect to the team's CI server or defect tracker. Which conclusion is best?

options.A: The CI server and defect tracker should both be replaced to fit the tool
options.B: Toolchain integration is a key criterion, so missing integrations weigh against the tool
options.C: Integrations are irrelevant, because results can always be copied by hand later
options.D: The tool should be chosen because integrations can never be built later

questions.explanation: Automation only pays off when results flow into the delivery process. Poor integration adds manual work and reduces the value of the tool.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: A cloud-based test tool would upload copies of application screenshots and test data to the vendor's servers. What should be done before choosing it?

options.A: Upload production data to check how the tool handles real cases
options.B: Carry out a security and data protection review of where data is stored and protected
options.C: Reject all cloud tools without evaluation, since cloud services are never safe
options.D: Approve it immediately, because cloud vendors always handle data securely

questions.explanation: Data leaving the organization must be assessed against security and privacy requirements. Blind approval or blanket rejection ignores the actual risk.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: A pilot required 200 hours to automate 50 test cases. The organization plans 500 more, but of similar complexity. How should the pilot data be used?

options.A: As a basis for estimates, adjusted for complexity and learning effects, with a contingency
options.B: Ignore it, because pilot data has no relationship to any later work in the program
options.C: Assume that the remaining tests can be done in a tenth of the pilot's time
options.D: Multiply the effort by ten, and treat the resulting number as exact

questions.explanation: Pilot data offers real evidence for estimating, though it needs adjustment and a margin for uncertainty. Exact multipliers or ignoring the data are unreliable.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: The budget is too small for both a commercial tool and adequate training. Which decision best protects the initiative?

options.A: Buy the tool and skip training, because people learn tools by themselves quickly
options.B: Cancel the initiative because it cannot be fully funded
options.C: Prioritize essentials, consider a cheaper tool or phasing, and keep the needed training
options.D: Spend everything on training and use no tool

questions.explanation: Both tools and skills are needed. Phasing and prioritization keep the initiative viable, whereas skipping training risks low adoption and poor quality.

questions.domain: Test Automation Resources
questions.question: Several teams write similar helper functions and keyword libraries separately. What is a sound resource strategy?

options.A: Let each team keep its own copies, since sharing always slows teams down
options.B: Prohibit helper functions, and require each test to contain all of its own code
options.C: Create a shared repository of reusable components with owners and documentation
options.D: Copy the components into each project by hand whenever they change

questions.explanation: Reuse reduces duplicated effort when shared components are owned, documented and versioned. Copies drift apart and duplicate maintenance.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: A team tests a mobile app only on emulators because they are cheap and quick, and users report device-specific defects. Which environment strategy is better?

options.A: Use only real devices for every test, whatever the cost and time
options.B: Ask users to test on their own devices before each release
options.C: Continue using only emulators, since real devices can never find additional defects
options.D: Use emulators for broad fast feedback and real devices for critical, device-specific checks

questions.explanation: Emulators are efficient but do not reproduce all hardware and vendor behavior. A balanced mix gives coverage at a reasonable cost.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Resetting a large test database by reloading it takes two hours, which delays the test runs. Which improvement is most suitable?

options.A: Ask the testers to delete the changed records by hand after each run
options.B: Stop resetting the database, and let the test data grow with every run
options.C: Reset the database only once every month, whatever the tests have changed
options.D: Use snapshots or fast restore, or smaller data sets, to reset the state quickly

questions.explanation: Fast restore or focused data sets deliver a known state without long waits. Skipping resets or manual clean-up makes results unreliable.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: A SaaS product must be tested against three supported versions of a database and two browsers. What is the best environment approach?

options.A: Test each combination manually once a year, before the annual release
options.B: Define a configuration matrix, automate provisioning, and run the relevant tests on each
options.C: Ask customers to report failures in the combinations that they happen to use
options.D: Test one combination only and assume that all the others behave the same way

questions.explanation: A matrix makes the required combinations explicit, and automation makes running them affordable and repeatable. Assumptions or annual checks leave gaps.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: A legacy system can be accessed by tests only during a short nightly window. Which strategy best increases automation value?

options.A: Schedule runs within the window, and virtualize the parts that are otherwise unavailable
options.B: Give up automation, since limited access makes any testing impossible
options.C: Ask the operators to extend the window to 24 hours regardless of their needs
options.D: Run the tests during the day even though the system is unavailable

questions.explanation: Working with the available window and simulating unavailable parts makes automated execution feasible. Ignoring availability or abandoning automation gives no benefit.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Build agents in the CI system cannot reach the test environment because of firewall rules, and tests fail on connection errors. What is the right response?

options.A: Disable the firewall on all networks to make the connection errors disappear
options.B: Retry the connections repeatedly until one of them happens to succeed
options.C: Move the tests to run only on individual laptops outside the corporate network
options.D: Agree and document the required access with the network team, and check connectivity

questions.explanation: Access requirements should be agreed and documented, then verified with checks. Removing security controls or relying on luck is not acceptable.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: Teams in three time zones share one test environment, and conflicts occur when they deploy at the same time. Which practice reduces this?

options.A: Requiring teams to phone each other before every deployment
options.B: Removing the environment and having teams test on production
options.C: A shared booking calendar or reservation system with clear deployment windows
options.D: A rule that the team in the first time zone may always use the environment

questions.explanation: Visible reservations coordinate access across time zones and prevent overlapping deployments. Fixed priority or phone calls do not scale.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: The team wants to test every pull request in a separate environment, but costs are a concern. Which approach is most balanced?

options.A: Skip testing pull requests to save on environment cost
options.B: Create a permanent full-size environment for each pull request, and keep all of them
options.C: Create short-lived, right-sized environments on demand, and remove them automatically after the tests
options.D: Test all pull requests in the same shared environment at the same time

questions.explanation: On-demand, right-sized and automatically removed environments provide isolation at limited cost. Permanent copies are expensive, and sharing loses isolation.

questions.domain: Test Automation Environments
questions.question: An engineer fixed a problem in the test environment by editing a setting by hand, and later runs behave differently from the documented setup. What is the best preventive measure?

options.A: Document manual changes in a private notebook only
options.B: Manage changes through code and pipelines, and rebuild environments periodically
options.C: Forbid all changes to environments, even for urgent fixes
options.D: Encourage engineers to make manual changes without recording them, to save time

questions.explanation: Code-managed changes and regular rebuilds keep the environment aligned with its definition. Bans or unrecorded changes are impractical or lose traceability.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Nobody clearly owns the CI pipeline: the QA team blames operations for failures, and operations blames the QA team. Which organizational step helps?

options.A: Let the pipeline run without any owner, so that nobody can be blamed for it
options.B: Give ownership to whichever person complains most often about the pipeline
options.C: Define pipeline ownership and responsibilities, with shared goals for handling failures
options.D: Remove the pipeline and return to manual builds and manual releases

questions.explanation: Clear responsibilities and shared goals ensure problems are fixed instead of debated. Ownerless or removed pipelines lose their benefits.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: The team wants to judge whether its automation strategy works for releases. Which metric is most informative in this respect?

options.A: Defects that escape to production, tracked over releases and related to the tests
options.B: The total number of automated test cases in the whole repository at each release
options.C: The number of test cases executed per hour on the busiest day of the year
options.D: The number of team members who have attended the automation training courses

questions.explanation: Escaped defects show what the strategy failed to catch, and their trend guides improvement. Counts of tests, throughput or training measure effort rather than effectiveness.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A remote team in another country needs to adopt the shared automation solution. Which rollout element helps most?

options.A: A local champion with training, access to support and clear documentation
options.B: A requirement to travel to the head office for a year
options.C: An email with instructions written in the language of the head office only
options.D: No support, so that the remote team learns to be independent

questions.explanation: Local support and accessible material lower the barriers for remote adoption. Distance without support leads to poor uptake.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A new environment is built through blue-green deployment. Which automated activity gives the best safety before switching traffic to it?

options.A: Switch traffic immediately, because blue-green deployments cannot fail
options.B: Switch the traffic first and run the tests afterward
options.C: Run smoke and critical-path checks on the new environment before switching traffic
options.D: Run the tests only against the old environment

questions.explanation: Verifying the new environment before the switch limits the impact of problems and keeps a rollback option. Testing after the switch or the wrong environment gives no protection.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Several teams resist a new mandatory automation approach, and the rollout stalls. Which action best addresses this?

options.A: Cancel the rollout and keep all teams in their current way of working
options.B: Send a short announcement, and assume the teams will accept the change
options.C: Threaten teams with sanctions if they do not comply by the end of the week
options.D: Have a visible sponsor explain the reasons, listen to concerns and adapt where justified

questions.explanation: Adoption is a change-management task. Sponsorship, dialogue and involvement build commitment, whereas coercion or a one-way message produces resistance.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: The automation rollout plan does not match the organization's annual budget cycle, and funding for the second phase is uncertain. What should be done?

options.A: Start phase two anyway without funding, and ask for the money later
options.B: Skip reporting results so that no one questions the funding
options.C: Align phases and business cases with budget cycles, and show phase one results
options.D: Cancel phase two, because funding uncertainty means it cannot succeed

questions.explanation: Aligning phases with funding rhythms and demonstrating value reduces the risk of a stalled program. Unfunded starts or hidden results weaken it.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Twenty teams in one code base each need automated pipelines, and building twenty different ones would duplicate effort. Which approach is better?

options.A: Let each team build a pipeline from scratch with no guidance
options.B: Use a single pipeline that is run by one person for all twenty teams
options.C: Force one identical pipeline on all teams with no room for adjustment
options.D: Provide shared pipeline templates that teams can adapt within agreed standards

questions.explanation: Templates give consistency and reuse while allowing needed variation. Total uniformity, no guidance or a single operator are inflexible or unscalable.

questions.domain: Organizational Deployment and Release Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Several teams release together on a release train. The release manager wants one view of quality. Which is a suitable approach?

options.A: Collect all teams' automated results in one report with agreed readiness criteria
options.B: Skip readiness criteria and release whenever the calendar says so
options.C: Ask each team to report verbally in a weekly meeting and nothing else
options.D: Use only the results of the largest team to decide for all of the teams

questions.explanation: Consolidated, comparable results with agreed criteria give a basis for decisions. Verbal or partial information is inconsistent, and calendar-only decisions ignore quality.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Only one engineer knows how a critical part of the automation works. Which practices reduce this risk?

options.A: Pair on tasks, rotate responsibilities, review code and document the design
options.B: Give that engineer more work in the area to keep the knowledge in one place
options.C: Prohibit other engineers from touching that part of the code
options.D: Wait until the engineer leaves and then recreate the knowledge

questions.explanation: Sharing knowledge through pairing, rotation, reviews and documentation reduces dependence. Concentrating or locking away knowledge increases the risk.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: New team members take months to become productive on the automation solution. Which measure helps most?

options.A: Asking them to read all of the source code before taking any tasks
options.B: Assigning them the most complex tasks from the beginning
options.C: Giving them access to the repository and no further guidance
options.D: A structured onboarding with documentation, starter tasks and a mentor

questions.explanation: Structured onboarding shortens the time to productivity. Little guidance, exhaustive reading or the hardest tasks slow learning and cause frustration.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: As test automation manager, you identify that the team may not meet the schedule because of a dependency on another department. What is the appropriate responsibility?

options.A: Ignore it until the schedule has been missed
options.B: Assign the entire blame to the other department in the next report
options.C: Record it as a risk, agree mitigation with stakeholders, and monitor it
options.D: Remove the affected work from the plan without telling anyone

questions.explanation: Managing risks and communicating them is part of the manager role. Ignoring, blaming or silently changing plans harms transparency.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: A skills assessment shows that the team is weak in API-level testing, although the strategy calls for more of it. What is the best action?

options.A: Provide targeted training or mentoring, or hire for the skill, and track progress
options.B: Assign API testing only to the people who have declined all training
options.C: Remove API testing from the strategy without discussing it with anyone
options.D: Continue with the plan and hope that the team learns without any support

questions.explanation: Assessments are used to close identified gaps. Targeted development or hiring aligns skills with strategy, whereas hope or dropping goals does not.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Engineers spend nearly all of their time on new tests, and the maintenance of existing scripts is neglected. What planning practice fixes this?

options.A: Let maintenance happen whenever someone happens to have spare time
options.B: Reserve capacity for maintenance and refactoring in every iteration
options.C: Perform maintenance only in the last week before the release
options.D: Assume that existing tests will never need any maintenance work

questions.explanation: Maintenance is a continuous need. Reserving capacity and estimating it prevents decay of the suite, whereas assumptions or leftovers do not.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: A vendor is paid by the number of hours worked on automation, and quality is inconsistent. Which contract measure is most effective?

options.A: Remove all review of the vendor's work so the vendor is free to decide
options.B: Tie payment and reviews to agreed outcomes such as maintainability and value
options.C: Measure the vendor only by the number of scripts that it delivers
options.D: Pay the vendor for more hours whenever problems occur in its deliverables

questions.explanation: Outcome and quality measures align incentives with value. Hours or script counts reward activity, not results.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: A group of automation engineers wants to start a community of practice. Which approach is likely to succeed?

options.A: Start without any sponsor and never share results outside of the group
options.B: Require attendance at daily three-hour meetings from every engineer
options.C: Restrict membership to managers so that decisions are made by them
options.D: Start lightweight with regular sessions, get sponsorship, and tackle real problems

questions.explanation: Communities thrive when they are useful and low-friction, with visible support. Heavy obligations, isolation or managers-only membership kill participation.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: After automation tasks were added, the team's velocity dropped, and stakeholders are unhappy. What is the best response?

options.A: Include automation tasks in planning and estimates, and explain the investment
options.B: Add automation work on top of the existing plan without adjusting deadlines
options.C: Hide the automation work and report the same velocity as before
options.D: Stop all automation tasks immediately so that velocity recovers

questions.explanation: Automation is work that takes capacity, so it needs to be planned and communicated as an investment. Hiding it or overloading the team leads to poor quality.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Nobody is sure who is responsible for providing and maintaining test data for automation, and tests keep failing on missing data. Which step resolves this?

options.A: Let each test create whatever data it wants, without any coordination
options.B: Ask the operations team to guess which data the tests will need
options.C: Remove the tests that depend on data
options.D: Define ownership for test data, and agree how it is created and refreshed

questions.explanation: Clear ownership and agreed processes make data available and reliable. Uncoordinated creation or guessing produces conflicts and gaps.

questions.domain: Roles, Skills, and Team Structures
questions.question: Testers and developers work in separate silos, and automated tests are written after the code is complete, often without hooks that would help. Which collaboration change is most effective?

options.A: Have testers wait until the developers have completely finished everything
options.B: Keep the teams separate and communicate only through defect reports
options.C: Ask developers to write all of the automated tests entirely on their own
options.D: Have testers and developers collaborate on design and implementation, e.g. by pairing

questions.explanation: Early collaboration builds testability and avoids rework. Sequential, isolated work leads to late discovery of obstacles.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Before starting an improvement program, the team wants to be able to show its effect later. What should it do first?

options.A: Measure the current state as a baseline, and pick the most valuable problem
options.B: Wait a year before measuring anything
options.C: Choose the changes that are easiest to implement and skip measuring
options.D: Start changing everything at once and compare with memories of the past

questions.explanation: A baseline makes improvement visible, and focusing on the most valuable problem yields impact. Simultaneous or unmeasured changes make results unclear.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Analysis shows that the same checks exist at UI, API and unit levels, which slows the suite without more coverage. What is the right action?

options.A: Delete the unit tests, because the UI tests already cover everything
options.B: Add further duplicates at every level, to be on the safe side of coverage
options.C: Keep all the tests as they are, since redundancy is always a benefit
options.D: Keep each check at the lowest suitable level and remove redundant higher-level tests

questions.explanation: Placing checks at the lowest suitable level gives faster, more stable feedback. Unmanaged duplication increases cost without adding protection.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: The automation framework's dependencies have not been updated in three years, and an upgrade is now a major risk. What would have avoided this?

options.A: Letting each engineer update dependencies whenever they like
options.B: Regular small, planned dependency updates verified by tests
options.C: Updating everything at once every five years
options.D: Never updating anything at all

questions.explanation: Small, regular updates keep changes manageable and risk low. Long gaps make upgrades large and risky, and uncontrolled updates cause instability.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: A serious defect reached production even though the automated regression suite passed. Which follow-up is most valuable?

options.A: Add the defect to the list of known issues and continue
options.B: Blame the tester who wrote the closest test and take no other action
options.C: Analyze why the suite missed it, add or adjust tests, and look for similar gaps
options.D: Remove the suite, since it obviously cannot protect the product

questions.explanation: Escaped defects reveal coverage or design gaps. Root cause analysis improves the suite, whereas blame, removal or ignoring the issue does not.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Retrospectives produce good ideas, but few are implemented, and the same problems recur. What improves the process?

options.A: Turn ideas into a few prioritized actions with owners and dates, then review them
options.B: Let one manager privately decide which of the ideas will count
options.C: Write all ideas on a board and simply leave them there for later
options.D: Hold retrospectives less often so that fewer ideas are generated in total

questions.explanation: Improvement needs follow-through. Prioritized, owned and reviewed actions make change happen, whereas fewer sessions or unmanaged lists do not.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Estimates for automation tasks are often wrong by a large margin. Which practice improves them over time?

options.A: Stop estimating altogether and simply work without any real plan
options.B: Use the estimate given by the most optimistic team member every time
options.C: Record actual effort, compare it with estimates, and refine later estimates
options.D: Always double the estimate without analyzing any of the results

questions.explanation: Learning from actuals calibrates estimates. Arbitrary factors, no planning or optimism alone do not improve accuracy.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Quick fixes have led to messy, duplicated automation code that is expensive to change. What strategy handles this automation debt?

options.A: Ignore the debt until the code stops working completely
options.B: Rewrite everything from scratch without evaluating what is valuable
options.C: Add more quick fixes to hide the problems in the code
options.D: Schedule regular refactoring and cleanup alongside new work, guided by reviews

questions.explanation: Debt is reduced by continuous, planned cleanup. Neglect makes it worse, wholesale rewrites are risky, and further quick fixes add to the problem.

questions.domain: Implementation and Improvement Strategies for Test Automation
questions.question: Reports show a steady 95 percent pass rate, and the team feels safe. Yet defects are escaping. What should the team check?

options.A: Whether the defects were reported on a working day
options.B: Whether pass rate is calculated in a different color
options.C: Whether the pass rate can be pushed to 100 percent by removing failing tests
options.D: Whether the passing tests are meaningful and cover the risky areas of the product

questions.explanation: A high pass rate can hide gaps if tests are weak or miss risk areas. Assessing coverage and test quality shows what confidence is justified.
